correctness.rationale: The difference body is explicitly a regular even polygon: for odd n, maximal vertex differences form a regular 2n-gon, while every nonmaximal difference lies inside its inball using cos(3x)<cos²x. Hence width is the exact cosine chamber; integrating two chamber pieces establishes mixed covariance. Differentiation and strict decay of sin t/t for 0<t<=pi/2 show C strictly decreases. Period averaging forces the endpoint negative; uniqueness follows by continuity. Centered Taylor expansion is uniform and yields the explicitly integrated quartic H(q)=(8-15q²(2-q)²)/360; its simple zero and H(1)/H(0)=-7/8 yield the asymptotics. Actual verify.py reconstructed n=3..12 polygon widths from vertices, tested five lags each and larger root approximations; 223 finite numerical regression checks passed. Finite checks are corroborative, not proof.

value.rationale: The covariance sign of two width measurements at prescribed angular separation expresses whether the second observation is positively or negatively informative relative to the first. Regular polygons are canonical models for orientation-sensitive geometric tomography. This theorem gives an exact global one-transition law and a universal nontrivial scaling profile, with sharp transition q*=1-sqrt(1-sqrt(8/15)) and limiting maximal anticorrelation -7/8, rather than simply recomputing the known variance, giving an arbitrary finite table, or a routine renaming. No downstream universality beyond regular polygons is assumed.
